solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Loafer's plan to get round Jack

indicators.note: the plan word encircles the sailor, so these words signal one piece wrapped around another

parts.note: a layout is a plan or arrangement
a jack tar is a sailor, and AB (able seaman) is the usual crossword sailor

explanation.surface: A lazy person's scheme to get the better of someone called Jack.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: an idler who lounges about and avoids work is a loafer.

clue.text: I am becoming unfit

parts.note: contracted to I'M
becoming in the sense of fitting or seemly, i.e. proper

explanation.surface: Someone admits they are getting out of shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becoming' looks like the verb of change, but here it is the adjective meaning seemly.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: something unsuitable or not fitting the occasion is unfit for it.

clue.text: Watch a pet's fancy ribbon

parts.note: ticker is slang for a watch

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or reworked, telling us to rearrange the letters of a pet

explanation.surface: A watch and a pet's decorative ribbon, perhaps on a collar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' rearranges A PET into TAPE.
explanation.definitionFit: The paper strip printed by old stock tickers is a narrow ribbon, also thrown in parades.

clue.text: Brightly-coloured pictures turning up on ship

indicators.note: in a down answer, turning up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: red is a bright colour
art means pictures collectively

explanation.surface: Colourful paintings appearing on board a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses REDART, giving TRADER.
explanation.definitionFit: A merchant vessel is called a trader, a ship carrying goods for commerce.

clue.text: Murderer, one put in gaol

indicators.note: the numeral is placed inside the prison word, signalling insertion

parts.note: can is slang for prison
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A killer, jailed.
explanation.walkthrough: Cain killed his brother Abel in Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible he is the first killer, slaying his brother Abel.

clue.text: Irritability on the outside?

definitions.meaning: read whimsically as the quality of being at the edge or border of something

explanation.surface: Is irritability something that shows on the outside?
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the word as edge plus -iness: being on the edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on edge means tense and irritable; the whimsical sense is being at the edge, i.e. the outside.

clue.text: Carrying nothing from part of south London

indicators.note: nothing is taken from the place name, so these words signal removal

parts.note: Tooting is a district of south London
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Hauling nothing away from a London neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' removes one O from TOOTING, a district of south London.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to tote is to carry, especially something heavy or a gun.

clue.text: Promise to put small amount of money on unfinished book

parts.note: P is a penny, a small coin

indicators.note: unfinished means the account book loses its final letter

parts.note: a ledger is an account book

explanation.surface: A vow to bet a little cash on a book not yet completed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' drops the last letter of LEDGER to give LEDGE; 'on' places P above it in the down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a solemn vow or undertaking is a pledge.

clue.text: Lots go under it

parts.note: auction lots are sold when the auctioneer's gavel falls: they go under it

explanation.surface: Plenty of things pass beneath it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lots' are auction items, and 'going under the hammer' means being sold at auction.
explanation.definitionFit: An auctioneer's gavel marks each sale; items sold are said to go under it.

clue.text: Remove the grain for harvest

indicators.note: remove here means move the letters again, rearranging the grain

explanation.surface: Instructions to strip out grain so it can be harvested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remove' is read as re-move: rearrange THE GRAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to gather in a crop is to harvest it.

clue.text: Nag or badger noisily desperate character

indicators.note: noisily means the word is heard rather than read, a sound-alike

parts.note: to badger is to harry or pester
Desperate Dan is a strongman in the British comic The Dandy

explanation.surface: Pester or hound a hopeless person loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: Desperate Dan is the cowboy hero of the long-running British children's comic The Dandy.
explanation.definitionFit: A nag is a scolding, bad-tempered old woman, which is what the word means.

clue.text: Over the Channel, no time for minority

parts.note: across the Channel in France, no is non
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: In France there is no time for minority groups.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal minority, being under age, is the old sense: the period before adulthood.

clue.text: Related short comedy story

parts.note: com is short for comedy, as in sitcom or romcom
a parable is a story with a moral

explanation.surface: A tale was told in the form of a brief comic sketch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Related' looks like the verb meaning told, but it is the definition: similar.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are related, akin or similar, can be compared to each other.

clue.text: Groundwork done by graduates one's completed

parts.note: BAs are Bachelors of Arts, graduates
one is, giving I (Roman one) and S (the 's)

explanation.surface: Preparation carried out by graduates, and one has finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' is one is: I plus S; 'completed' simply says the build is done.
explanation.definitionFit: A foundation or groundwork is the basis on which something rests.

clue.text: Kitty's registered in hotels and loiters around

indicators.note: around means the letters are moved about, all mixed together

explanation.surface: A cat signs in at hotels and lingers about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' is the anagram signal; 'Kitty' suggests a pool of money, but here it is a cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A tortoiseshell is a cat with mottled black and ginger fur, so it is an example of a kitty.

clue.text: Be hostile to it being included on the other side

indicators.note: it is included within the word for resist, so the pronoun goes inside

parts.note: to oppose is to be against or hostile to

explanation.surface: Resisting something that is part of the rival faction.
explanation.definitionFit: Across from or facing means on the far or other side, a synonym.

clue.text: Drum or trumpet perhaps making connection

definitions.meaning: an eardrum or an ear trumpet
wiring to the ground, an electrical connection

explanation.surface: A musical instrument forming a link.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense splits the word as EAR THING: eardrums and ear trumpets are both things of the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: In electrics, grounding a circuit connects it to the ground for safety.

clue.text: A rapidly deteriorating cutter

indicators.note: deteriorating means breaking down, so the letters fall apart and reform

explanation.surface: A blade that is quickly getting worse.
explanation.definitionFit: A gem cutter or engraver of precious stones is called a lapidary.

clue.text: Polish or another language on the radio

indicators.note: radio is heard, so these words signal a sound-alike

parts.note: Finnish is the language of Finland

explanation.surface: Polish, or some other tongue, broadcast on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the language from Poland, but is the verb or noun for a shine.
explanation.definitionFit: A glossy surface coating or final burnish is a polish, a synonym.

clue.text: Allowed nothing to be put over beam

indicators.note: put over means turned over, so the pair of words is read backwards

parts.note: let means allowed
nil is nothing

explanation.surface: Permitted nothing to be placed above a timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be put over' reverses LETNIL as a whole, giving LINTEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A horizontal support above a door or window is a type of beam.

clue.text: Job and Psalms perhaps contracted extra comment

parts.note: a post is a job

indicators.note: contracted means shortened, so the end of the word is cut off

parts.note: Psalms is a book of scripture

explanation.surface: Biblical books like Job and Psalms, abbreviated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Job' looks like the biblical book beside Psalms, but it means a post; 'contracted' trims SCRIPTURE to SCRIPT.
explanation.definitionFit: An addition at the end of a letter, the P.S., is an extra remark.

clue.text: Watch Second Coming

parts.note: an entry is a coming in

explanation.surface: Look out for the Second Coming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second Coming' suggests the religious event, but splits into S and ENTRY.
explanation.definitionFit: A guard keeping watch is a sentry; the watch is a body of guards.

clue.text: Desire bride's address after party

indicators.note: after means the bride's words follow the party word

parts.note: Lib is short for Liberal, a political party
what a bride says at the altar: I do

explanation.surface: Longing for the bride's speech once the reception is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party' looks like a celebration but is the political Liberal party, LIB.
explanation.definitionFit: Sexual appetite or drive is libido, a kind of desire.

clue.text: Cooler overhead

parts.note: something above one's head that keeps one cool, such as a parasol

explanation.surface: A cooling device mounted above.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooler' suggests a fan or air conditioner; the device is a parasol held overhead.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasol or awning keeps the sun off, and so keeps one cool from above.

clue.text: Drive off — no time to race

indicators.note: no time means the time letter is removed

parts.note: to shoot is to race or dash

explanation.surface: Speed away, with no time to dash.
explanation.definitionFit: Waving a cat or bird away with a cry chases it off, i.e. drives it off.

clue.text: Old film star lush wants to eat less food for a start

indicators.note: for a start puts the dieting word at the beginning

parts.note: to diet is to eat less
rich and lush both mean luxuriant

explanation.surface: A boozy old actress wants to cut back on food at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lush' looks like a drunkard but means rich; Marlene Dietrich was a German-American film star.
explanation.definitionFit: Marlene was a screen idol of the 1930s and 1940s, an actress of classic cinema.

clue.text: Get exhausted as boring career comes first

indicators.note: comes first places the running word ahead of the dull word

parts.note: to career is to rush or run
dry means dull or boring

explanation.surface: Feeling drained because a tedious job takes priority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'career' looks like a job but is the verb meaning rush.
explanation.definitionFit: A well or supply that empties is used up, the idiom for running out.

clue.text: Quartz coming from Ceylon and Chad

indicators.note: the letters come out of the two country names, reformed into a new word

explanation.surface: A mineral that originates in Sri Lanka and Chad.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a cryptocrystalline form of silica, a variety of the mineral family that includes agate.
